title: feat(spec,lint): a form's thank-you panel names the record's engine-generated fields, and the public submit answer has a declared shape

Clause-②: yes (widening)

Skills-docs: follow-up owed — content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx and content/docs/ui/forms.mdx (the thank-you panel's `{{record.field_name}}` slot, taught once the server fills the answer and the Console fills the tokens; teaching it now would advertise a panel that still prints the token text); no `skills/**` page names the thank-you panel's text (`git grep -n "thank-you" -- skills/` is empty)

domain:spec#1 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibwKTredm7FjB4Z6DeX

This is the spec half of ruling B (ruling record 6545210989). The server half (`POST /forms/SLUG/submit` fills `fields`) and the ui half (`FormPage.tsx` fills the tokens) follow on their own cards, which the seat files once this PR is up.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：公开表单的「提交成功」面板（`thank-you` 的 `title` / `message`）可以用 `{{record.字段名}}` 引用刚提交的那条记录的字段，但只允许引擎在插入时自动生成的字段（目前就是自动编号 `autonumber`，比如案件号）。同时在 spec 里声明了公开表单提交接口的返回形状：`id`，加上面板引用到的那几个字段，别的什么都不带。
- **为什么改**：web-to-case 的访客提交后看不到自己的案件号。按裁决 B，只放引擎生成的字段，因为其它字段的值可能是 hook 从匿名访客无权读取的记录里算出来的，不能回显给匿名页面。
- **风险与回滚**：低。引用写法和 `redirect` 的 `url` 是同一个记号；写错形状（`{record.x}`、`{{ record.x }}`、`{{case_number}}`）在解析时被拒并说明正确写法；引用了非自动编号字段，在 `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` 和 view、page 的发布门被拒，并点名字段和类型。现有示例、hotcrm 里没有任何面板文字带花括号（实测为零）。回滚即 revert。
- **先看**：`packages/lint/src/validate-thank-you-record-fields.ts`（判定规则，只读 `RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES`）；`packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`（`THANK_YOU_TEXT_RE`、`checkThankYouText`、`thankYouRecordFieldNames`）；`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`（`PublicFormSubmitResponseSchema`）。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/validate-thank-you-record-fields.test.ts`，预期 16/16 通过：自动编号字段放行，文本字段、公式字段、未声明字段、系统列各被拒并点名类型；把类型集合在测试里放宽一种类型即放行，无需改规则。
- **需要你做的**：批准三个新名字（见下文 Names for approval），其余无，席位落地。

## What changes

### 1. The slot (`@objectstack/spec`, `ui/view.zod.ts`)

The `thank-you` member's `title` and `message` stay `z.string()`: the renderer receives the text the author wrote. Each now carries a `.regex(THANK_YOU_TEXT_RE)`: every brace in the text must belong to a well-formed `{{record.field_name}}` token. That is the same token the `redirect` member's `url` takes (`SUBMIT_REDIRECT_URL_TOKEN_RE`), so there is one grammar and no second dialect.

- **A malformed token is refused on its own terms**, in the style of `checkSubmitRedirectUrl`. `checkThankYouText` words the refusal from the input: it names the member (`title` or `message`), quotes the offending text, and gives the one spelling (`{{record.case_number}}`). It also says braces belong to that token alone, and that only an engine-generated field may be named.
- **A regex, not a refine.** A `.regex()` projects into the published JSON Schema as a `pattern`, so the file carries the shape too. That means no new `x-dropped-refinements` site and no `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` row. The two alternatives in the pattern start on disjoint characters, so matching is linear.
- **`thankYouRecordFieldNames(submitBehavior)`** is the one reading of which fields a panel names: `title` then `message`, each name once, in order of first appearance, and `[]` for any other kind. It is a pure function of the block. The lint rule judges exactly these names, and the server half fills exactly these fields.
- The two members gain a `.describe()` that states the slot and its limit. The union's own describe, which is projected into the governed `skills/objectstack-ui/references/react-blocks.md`, is unchanged, so this PR touches no governed surface.

### 2. The authoring check (`@objectstack/lint`, `validate-thank-you-record-fields.ts`)

- **Where it lives.** I measured whether the redirect token's "declared record fields" rule is cross-checked anywhere. It is not: no lint rule reads `submitBehavior.url`, and the `view.zod.ts` docblock only names the reference-integrity family as the right layer. The nearest existing site that resolves a form's object fields is `validate-public-form-file-fields.ts`. The new rule sits beside it, with the same registration: gating, all three commands, the runtime publish gate. It resolves the form's object with the same `anonymousFormObjectName` the anonymous doors use.
- **One source.** A name is admitted only when its field's type is in `RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES` (`data/field.zod.ts`, today `autonumber`). The rule spells no field type of its own. It takes the set as a defaulted parameter only so a test can widen it as a double: the spec dist is externalised in lint's tests, so it cannot be module-mocked.
- **What is refused,** naming the field, its type and the reason (a value a hook may have set from records the anonymous grant cannot read):
  - a declared field of any other type (`text`, `formula`, …);
  - a registry-injected column (`created_at`, `owner_id`, `id`), which is injected, not engine-numbered;
  - a name the object does not declare (the panel would print nothing).
- **Which forms.** Every form that carries a `thank-you` panel, public or not: the bare form-view shape, the nested `form`, every `formViews` entry, the flattened `config` of a `viewKind: 'form'` item, and a page `object-form` component (`properties.submitBehavior`, object from `properties.objectName`, else the page walk's binding). The slot is one slot with one admission. A form that is internal today becomes public by flipping its `sharing`, and that is a write this rule would otherwise never see again.
- **Runtime publish gate:** `runtimeTypes: ['view', 'page']`. Both snapshots carry `objects` as context, which is every input the rule reads. `object` is not declared, for the reason the file-field rule gives: an object write's snapshot carries no views or pages.
- A form whose object does not resolve in the stack is not judged, the same boundary the file-field rule draws.

### 3. The answer shape (`@objectstack/spec`, `api/protocol.zod.ts`)

I measured whether any spec schema names the `POST /forms/:slug/submit` answer. None does: `rest-route-ledger.ts` lists the route with no `responseSchema`. `PublicFormSubmitResponseSchema` now sits next to `CreateDataResponseSchema`:

- `id: string`;
- `fields` (optional): a map from field name to a string or number value, holding exactly the named fields' stored values, present only when the panel names at least one;
- **`.strict()`,** so a key beyond these two is a conformance failure rather than a silent widening of what an anonymous caller is shown.

The server half fills it and names it as the route's `responseSchema`. ⛔ `packages/rest/src/form-routes.ts` is untouched here.

### Names for approval

The order asks for Tesla's approval of every new name. These are proposals; renaming before merge is a mechanical edit.

| Name | Kind | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `PublicFormSubmitResponseSchema` (type `PublicFormSubmitResponse`) | REST answer schema | `@objectstack/spec/api` |
| `fields` | key on that answer | the map of named field values |
| `thankYouRecordFieldNames` | pure helper | `@objectstack/spec/ui` |
| `thank-you-record-field` / `validateThankYouRecordFields` | lint rule id / function | `@objectstack/lint` |

`THANK_YOU_TEXT_RE` and `checkThankYouText` are module-private.

## Tests

- **Parse** (`packages/spec/src/ui/view-submit-thank-you-record-slot.test.ts`, 15):
  - A `message` with `{{record.case_number}}` parses, and the text arrives verbatim. Title tokens, several tokens, token-free text and an empty panel all parse.
  - Refused, each naming the offender and the one spelling, at the member's path: `{record.x}`, `{{ record.x }}`, `{{case_number}}`, an uppercase segment, a dotted path, and a stray `}`.
  - The refusal carries no tracker id or date. The published JSON Schema carries the shape as a `pattern`.
  - `thankYouRecordFieldNames` reads title then message, each once, and reads only well-formed tokens. It answers `[]` for other kinds and for non-objects.
- **Answer schema** (`packages/spec/src/api/public-form-submit-response.test.ts`, 4): it accepts `{ id }` and `{ id, fields: { case_number } }`. It refuses another top-level key (`unrecognized_keys`), a missing `id` and a non-scalar value.
- **Authoring check** (`packages/lint/src/validate-thank-you-record-fields.test.ts`, 16):
  - On a fixture object, an `autonumber` token passes. `text` and `formula` tokens are refused, and the message names the field and its type. An undeclared name and the injected `created_at` / `id` are refused too.
  - Every form shape is judged: `form`, `formViews.*`, the `viewKind: 'form'` config, the bare form view, a public form, and a page `object-form`. A list-shaped `fields` is read, and the object resolves from the view.
  - **One source:** widening `RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES` in a test double (`+ 'formula'`) admits the formula token with no other edit. The rule source imports the set from `@objectstack/spec/data` and spells no `'autonumber'`.
  - Registration is pinned: gating, three commands, `['view', 'page']`. The runtime publish gate refuses a `view` write naming a text field and admits the same write naming the autonumber field.
- **Existing pins updated:**
  - The publish-gate rule rosters name the new rule in `authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts`, `runtime-gate.test.ts` (3 sites) and `runtime-gate.page-visibility-predicate-writes.test.ts` (2 sites).
  - `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` pins `PublicFormSubmitResponseSchema` as isomorphic (805 → 806, with the reason in the count's ledger comment).

The type gate is the anchor `if (type !== undefined && admitted.has(type)) return undefined;`, which went x1 → x0, replaced by an unconditional `return undefined;`.

- Blob `014ba032cba7` → `e040658efab9`.
- `validate-thank-you-record-fields.test.ts`: 9 failed | 7 passed. The text and formula refusals, every form-shape case, the page case, the one-source widening case and the runtime gate's refusal all went red.
- Restored: blob `014ba032cba7` = HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- **A brace in panel text is now refused unless it is the token.** Before this PR, `title` / `message` accepted any text. Text with a brace that is not a well-formed token (a literal `{`, `{{ x }}`) now fails to parse. The order asked for this, mirroring the redirect refine. I measured the corpus: no authored `thank-you` title or message in `examples/`, the non-test `packages/` sources or `hotcrm` contains a brace. I copied the claim's declaration lines (`yes (widening)`, `added`) unchanged. The seat decides whether this face changes the Clause-② arm.
- **`{{record.id}}` is refused.** `id` is not a `RUNTIME_OWNED_FIELD_TYPES` type. The answer already carries `id` at the top, so admitting it would be a separate decision.
- **Translations are not judged.** The i18n checks (`validate-translation-references.ts`) read only the key address of `…submitBehavior.title/message`, never its text, so a token in the text breaks no translation check (measured). A translated panel could name a field the base text does not name. The server half fills only the base text's names, so such a token would print as written; it never leaks. Whether to judge translated text is the ui/server cards' question.
- **An `object` write is not re-judged.** An object write's snapshot carries no views or pages, so retyping a named field under a published panel is caught by the CLI commands and by the form's next publish. This is the same boundary as the file-field rule.
- Until the server and ui halves land, a panel that names a field shows the token text verbatim. The changeset says so.
